messages.subject: Re: unexpected behavior of scale_fill_manual
parts:
I'm no expert, but the following should be a workaround:

df.na = df
df.na[2, 2] = NA
df.na$col = c("red", "green", "blue")
seln = !is.na(df.na[,2])

ggplot(df.na[seln,], aes(names, values, fill=names, label=values)) + geom_bar(stat="identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values=df.na$col[seln]) + geom_text(vjust=-0.5)



On Thursday, 23 May 2013 02:34:28 UTC+1, mandr...@gmail.com wrote:

I'm not sure if I've found a bug, or if I'm just not understanding something. I am seeing strange behavior of scale_fill_manual() with an ordered factor when used in combination with geom_text(), but only when there is missing data.

Here is a sort-of-minimal reproducible example.

df <- data.frame(names=c("Foo", "Bar", "Aardvark"), values=1:3)
df$names <- factor(df$names, as.character(df$names), ordered=T)

ggplot(df, aes(names, values, fill=names, label=values)) + geom_bar(stat="identity") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("red", "green", "blue")) + geom_text(vjust=-0.5)

With no missing data, the behavior is exactly what I expect: the x axis has the levels arranged as determined by the ordering of the levels, as are the fill colors (see weird1.png). However, if I introduce missing data

df.na <- df
df.na[2, 2] <- NA
ggplot(df.na, aes(names, values, fill=names, label=values)) + geom_bar(stat="identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("red", "green", "blue")) + geom_text(vjust=-0.5)

then suddenly the order of the fill colors changes to alphabetic, even though the order along the x axis is unchanged (see weird2.png).

This seems to have something to do with geom_text(), as removing it restores the order, but now it's behaving as if the "Bar" level wasn't even there:

ggplot(df.na, aes(names, values, fill=names, label=values)) + geom_bar(stat="identity") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("red", "green", "blue"))

(see weird3.png).

In my application, I think I can use the simple workaround of just rearranging the color vector appropriately, but it still would be nice to understand what's going on here.

Anybody have any ideas?

Thanks in advance,

Mike

I'm no expert either, but here is how I would do it:

colors <- c("red", "green", "blue")
names(colors) <- levels(df.na$name)
ggplot(df.na, aes(names, values, fill=names, label=values)) + geom_bar(stat="identity") +

geom_text(vjust=-0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=colors)

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: unexpected behavior of scale_fill_manual
parts:
Here are a couple of other thoughts.

I thought Ista's idea should have worked inside scale_fill_manual() as
follows, but it doesn't:

# Fails

ggplot(df.na, aes(names, values, fill=names, label=values)) +
geom_bar(stat="identity") +

# However, a more brute force approach (not recommended) does:

ggplot(df.na, aes(names, values, fill = names)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
scale_fill_manual(values=c("Foo" = "red",
"Bar" = "green",
"Aardvark" = "blue")) +
geom_text(aes(label = values), vjust=-0.5)

AFAICS, these should be equivalent specifications, and I'm rather
curious as to why the first specification fails, especially since the
level associated with the missing value is not dropped from the graph.

An alternative approach is to define the colors as a factor in the
original data frame and use scale_fill_identity(); this works as
expected in both cases.

df2 <- df

df2$col <- c("red", "green", "blue")

ggplot(df2, aes(names, values, fill = col)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
geom_text(aes(label = values), vjust = -0.5) +
scale_fill_identity(guide = "legend")

df2.na <- df2
df2.na[2, 2] <- NA
ggplot(df2.na, aes(names, values, fill = col)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
geom_text(aes(label = values), vjust = -0.5) +
scale_fill_identity(guide = "legend")

Dennis
